articles.description:
New!
 
Improvement
  
We're excited to announce a major enhancement to your experience with our own payment solution, SmilyPay. Now, setting up your SmilyPay account is easier than ever, directly from your Smily dashboard. Here's what you can expect:
What's New?
Direct Signup: You can now create and manage SmilyPay accounts directly from your Smily account settings under Settings > Payments section.
Multiple Accounts: Need more than one account? No problem! Autonomously create as many SmilyPay accounts as you need.
Guided Setup: Our intuitive, step-by-step process will guide you through providing all the necessary information.
Why SmilyPay?
Tailored for You: SmilyPay is designed specifically for the payment needs of property managers and owners.
Cost-Effective: Enjoy lower transaction fees for European card transactions compared to Stripe.
Ready to Get Started?
Head over to your Smily account settings now and start setting up your SmilyPay accounts with ease. Join the many property managers already benefiting from a more efficient and cost-effective payment solution.
articles.title: Creating a new SmilyPay account is now super simple and efficient!

articles.author: Megan, Product Manager
articles.description:
Improvement
  
We've made some small but impactful changes to the Smily payment page. Enjoy an improved Meta title, a clearer display of discounts, better visibility of damage deposits, and a refined display of centimes. 
Check them out below:
The Meta title is now "Provide Payment Information" instead of "Smily"


Euro cents are now displayed in the same font as other digits


The damage deposit is no longer included in the balance amount due, but is displayed separately


Discounts are now displayed in negative, making it much clearer for guests when they're getting a great deal




Stay tuned for more improvements to the payment page, coming soon!
articles.title: Enhancements to the Smily Payment Page

articles.author: Megan, Product Manager
articles.description:
New!
  
Discover how SmilyPay’s latest feature simplifies your financial reconciliation process!
We recently added a Finance section to Smily, to help you to track and reconcile your payouts from SmilyPay. 
Now, you can export the Completed Payouts Report from the Finance section as a CSV file. This new feature makes payment reconciliation quick and easy!
articles.title: New: export your SmilyPay payouts!

articles.author: Basile, Product Manager
articles.description:
New!
  
Are you looking to maximize your revenue and streamline your booking management? :) 
Smily is thrilled to announce the global release of our Non-Refundable Rate Synchronization feature with Booking.com now available directly from your Smily booking' app.
Why consider non-refundable rates?
Creating and managing non-refundable rates directly on Booking.com has always been a powerful strategy for securing guaranteed income. Now, with Smily's latest feature, you can set up these rates effortlessly, directly through the Smily interface, giving you more control and ease of setup.
Benefits of Non-Refundable Rates:
Secure more bookings: Attract guests who are sure about their travel plans by offering a percentage discount for non-refundable rates.
Reduce cancellations: Minimize the risk of last-minute cancellations, ensuring your earnings are protected.
Flexibility: Choose full or partial synchronization based on your needs, with the ability to manage multiple rates seamlessly.
How does it work?
Enable the Feature: 
Switch the non-refundable rates to "Yes" in your Smily settings under the Booking.com apps via the new "Non-Refundable option" in the Change Settings form of the property.


You can enable it by property or do a bulk edit from the button below > Apply for existing rentals.





Set Your Discount: Decide on the percentage discount for this rate, providing attractive pricing to your guests.


Synchronize and Go: Save your changes, and let Smily handle the synchronization with Booking.com using our new API integration.


Enable it today and start reaping the benefits!
Your Smily team
articles.title: Introducing non-refundable rate synchronization with Booking.com

articles.description:
Description: SCIM group name disclosure via the ACL editor
What happened?
The ACL editor in the admin console did not check SCIM
group names in the ACL rules against the tailnet name. This allowed tailnet A
to use SCIM groups from tailnet B in their ACL rules. A malicious user in
tailnet A could not gain access to target tailnet B this way. However, they
could use the fact that ACLs get saved without warnings to learn about valid
SCIM group names in other tailnets.
This issue was fixed on July 19th, 2024. A user trying to save ACLs with SCIM
group names from other tailnets will always receive a warning that these groups
do not exist, even if they do exist in other tailnets.
Who was affected?
None of the existing tailnets' ACLs appear to use SCIM group names from other
tailnets maliciously. A handful of customers used the wrong SCIM group names
from their production tailnets in their test tailnets by accident.
What was the impact?
A malicious user could learn about SCIM group names used in other tailnets.
What do I need to do?
No action is required.
articles.title: TS-2024-011

articles.description:
Description: Accidental ACL edits due to browser caching
What happened?
When switching tailnets in the admin console, an Admin user
could overwrite the ACLs of one tailnet with pending changes to ACLs
from another tailnet.
When a user has unsaved ACL changes in the admin console, those changes are
cached in browser storage. If this user is a member of multiple tailnets,
tailnet A and tailnet B, and is editing ACLs for tailnet A, using the tailnet
switcher in the top-right corner of the page would not clear the cached ACL
changes correctly. In some rare cases, saving ACLs of tailnet B after the
switch would use the cached ACL contents from tailnet A.
A user can be an Admin in multiple tailnets when they use GitHub to log in, and are a member of GitHub organizations, or the user is invited to another tailnet and granted the Admin role.
Tailnet switching in the admin console was added on May 22nd, 2023. We fixed
this bug on July 17th, 2024.
Who was affected?
Any user who is an Admin in multiple tailnets and edited ACLs in the admin
console between May 22, 2023 and July 17th, 2024 could trigger this bug after
switching the active tailnet.
What was the impact?
An Admin user could overwrite the ACLs of one tailnet with ACLs from another
tailnet.
What do I need to do?
If you are an Admin of multiple tailnets using the same login name, review the
ACLs in your tailnets for correctness.
articles.title: TS-2024-010

articles.description:
Incident began at 2024-07-30 14:05 and ended at 2024-07-30 17:10 (times are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)).

Incident Report

Summary

On Tuesday, 30 July 2024, Gmail experienced increased error rates and delivery delays for a duration of 3 hours and 5 minutes.

To our Gmail users who were impacted by these issues, we sincerely apologize. This is not the level of quality and reliability we strive to offer you, and we are taking immediate steps to improve the platform’s performance and availability.

Root Cause

Google engineers have determined that the increased error rates and delivery delays were due to unrelated root causes.

Email Delivery Delays

On Tuesday, 30 July 2024, at 07:05 US/Pacific, a series of fiberlines which carry Gmail in-flight traffic were unintentionally disabled between Google's US and European data centers as part of routine maintenance.

Increased Error Rates

On Tuesday, 30 July 2024, at 08:00 US/Pacific, a non-critical process responsible for batch data processing started generating an increased volume of traffic which overloaded Gmail’s back-end system.

Remediation and Prevention

Email Delivery Delays

Google engineers were alerted of the incident through automated alert systems on Tuesday, 30 July 2024 at 07:14 US/Pacific and immediately began an investigation. By 07:34 US/Pacific, engineers performed a change to mitigate congestion/throttling which rerouted traffic to available servers for processing.

Increased Error Rates

Google engineers were alerted of the incident through automated alert systems on Tuesday, 30 July 2024 at 08:00 US/Pacific and immediately began an investigation. The issue self-resolved on Tuesday, 30 July 2024 at 10:10 US/Pacific, and errors were trending down to the baseline. The engineers identified and made the necessary changes to avoid a repeat of the issue at 10:30 US/Pacific.

Google is committed to preventing a repeat of this issue in the future and is completing the following actions:

  • Audit and test our traffic priority labels and storage system behavior to ensure that background traffic cannot overload the system.
  • Audit/test error propagation to make sure the routing layer responds adequately to error conditions.

Google is committed to quickly and continually improving our technology and operations to prevent service disruptions. We appreciate your patience and apologize again for the impact to your organization. We thank you for your business.

Detailed Description of Impact

Email Delivery Delays On July 30, 2024 07:05 to 08:00 US/Pacific, some emails were delayed between 10-20 minutes.

Increased Error Rates On July 30, 2024 07:46 to 10:10 US/Pacific, some users received potentially visible errors:

  • An error message banner with a valid retry button for users to manually retry the next Gmail web server - “Oops… the system encountered a problem (#2014)”

Affected products: Gmail

Issue Summary:
On Thursday, July 11, 2024, from 12:10 PM PDT to 12:12 PM PDT, a number of users had trouble loading messages in Slack.

Our internal monitoring systems alerted us of the unexpected spike in error rates which prompted our incident response processes to begin. Through our investigation, we determined that a recent data migration caused an unexpected influx of client reloads, which temporarily overwhelmed the database responsible for servicing the affected API calls.

As a result, an automated safety measure temporarily paused traffic until the database returned to a healthy state. Once error rates returned to normal, users were no longer experiencing trouble.
articles.title: Incident: Intermittent performance issues using Slack

articles.description:
Issue summary:
From 7:13 PM PDT on July 2, 2024 to 2:38 PM PDT on July 3, 2024, some users experienced issues loading threads in Slack.

We traced the issue to one of our databases. Repeated API calls related to threads from one org caused the database responsible for storing that thread to become overwhelmed. This overload affected other users accessing the same database, causing congestion, which prevented them from using it effectively and created further unexpected timeouts.

As an immediate mitigation step, we halted all traffic from users using that API call in order to retrieve the thread from the database which allowed our systems to catch-up. Once traffic started flowing at a reasonable rate again, we reinstated the API call for all users and disallowed the thread that initially caused an issue. This resolved the issue for all impacted users.

We've now added additional code to the problematic thread to bypass this particular API so that any unwanted traffic congestion can be mediated.
articles.title: Incident: Issues loading threads

Issue Summary:
On June 24, 2024 from 11:25AM PDT to July 3, 2024 11:30AM PDT, users were unable to post in some channels due to an "Only some people can post" message on iOS as if the channel was made announcement-only. This initially was handled as a bug, however, the issue began to unexpectedly impact more users. Out of an abundance of caution, we promptly activated our incident response processes to expedite our investigation.

We determined this issue was presenting only temporarily for most users and was often resolved by switching channels, clearing app cache, or by force-closing the app and re-launching.

A fix was implemented in version 24.07.10 of the iOS app to restore channel posting functionality, resolving the issue for affected users. Updating the app is recommended in order to capture the fix.
